newsitem.title: USA: Airline stocks soften on Merrill downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Airline stocks soften on Merrill downgrade.

text.p: Airline stocks softened Thursday as investors viewed Merrill Lynch's downgrade of two carriers as a reason to unload and take profits, analysts said.

Merrill Lynch cut UAL Corp to near-term neutral from buy and to long-term accumulate from buy. Merrill also cut Alaska Air Group Inc to near-term neutral from accumulate and to long-term accumulate from buy. Additional details were not immediately available.

Analysts said Merrill's downgrade of United, the nation's largest airline, set the tone for Thursday's session. The Dow Jones Transportation Average slipped 1.56 percent or about 40 points to 2533, falling slightly more than the 1.11 percent drop in the Dow industrials.

Airline stock had risen steady in the weeks ahead of their robust first quarter earnings. Companies such as Delta Air Lines Inc and UAL Corp hit new 52-week highs before sliding as investors took profits on the company's record earnings.
Stocks have fallen further as some analysts suggested the airlines have little potential for a near-term upswing.

"These stocks, in general, have really been at near-high levels. The '97 numbers are really fairly valued. And you have to look to the 1998 numbers before they begin to look undervalued," said Helane Becker, an analyst at Smith Barney.
UAL lost 3-1/8 to 71-1/4, AMR shed 2-3/8 to 90-3/4 and US Airways Group Inc slipped 1-1/8 to 31-1/4. Alaska Air lost 1 to 23-7/8.
